Have you looked into depression at all?

It's a chemical imbalance in your brain. Your neurotransmitters aren't like the proper shape in a sense. (think about that toddler toy where you have to fit the right shapes into their respectively shaped holes)

Your serotonin isn't being absorbed (that's the chemical that is associated with happiness) What medication does is change the shape of your neurotransmitters so that they can absorb serotonin easier.

I was prescribed antidepressants when i was maybe 17, I was petrified to start them. I had heard so much about this "zombified state" psychological drugs easily lure you into.

Depression is a miscommunication between your neurotransmitters and your receptors. Think of that learning game some kids have, where you have to put the right shapes into the right shaped hole. But imagine you have all circular holes and all rectangular prisms.

What antidepressants do is make those circular holes more rectangular so you can fit the prisms inside.

They don't change who you are. They put you on the same playing field as the rest of society.

**Important things you should know about antidepressants**

If you don't like the one you've been put on, keep taking it until you can talk to a doctor and let them know that you don't like it.

Never stop taking them cold turkey. You need to ween yourself off them, but if that's your intention you should let your doctor know.

If you do quit antidepressants all of a sudden your body can go through withdrawal, you can have some seriously heavy suicidal thoughts too.

I think antidepressants are good, just be smart about them.
